title: Separate registration decisions from the professions' own interests
action: Reform the structure and governance of the national bodies and colleges that set registration, accreditation and scope-of-practice rules, so that decisions about entry and scope are not made by people with an interest in limiting competition from new entrants or other professions.
why: When incumbent practitioners control entry and scope, rules can protect them rather than patients, limiting the supply of practitioners and the use of nurses and pharmacists for simpler care.

evidence.source: National Competition Policy: modelling proposed reforms
evidence.quote: Reform the structure and governance of national professional bodies that make occupational registration and licensing decisions to address conflicts of interest.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: Advancing Prosperity, Recommendations and Reform Directives
evidence.quote: Australian governments should work with the relevant regulators to re-examine boundary issues relating to occupational licences.
